Messages.Author: Derek S. Ray
Messages.Body:
On Thu, 27 May 1999 19:25:01 GMT, "Kristyl Meth"
<dapa...@riderlaw.com> wrote:

>Can anyone direct me to a link or post a decent pitch deck using Brujah or
>any other non-Sabbat clan? It's one type of deck I haven't tried yet, and
>I'd like to see an example to determine if I've got enough of the right
>cards...

oo, that'd be my cue, I think. Hold on:

Deck name: Hoo Flung Junk

Crypt: (12 cards)
1 Akram (Brujah, 8, CE po, Primogen)
1 Anvil (Brujah, 6, CE PO, Primogen)
1 Black Cat (Brujah, 5, po CE)
1 Donal O'Connor (Brujah, 8, CE PO, Prince)
1 Dre, Leader of the Cold Dawn (Brujah, 3, ce po)
1 Jacko (Brujah Antitribu, 8, CE PO)
1 Jacob Bragg (Brujah Antitribu, 3, ce po)
2 Jimmy Dunn (Pander, 4, PO CE)
1 Radeyah (Toreador, 6, CE po)
1 Rigby, Crusade Vanguard (Brujah Antitribu, 5, CE po)
1 Volker, The Puppet Prince (Brujah, 5, CE po, Prince)

If you use one Jimmy, of course, you have to use two. =) Almost
everyone in here is celerity-positive, and the lack of superior POT
doesn't really hurt this deck much, since the Lids and Blurs are where
your damage will come from. I considered duplicating vampires and
found that when I put in 2 of, say, Anvil, and dumped Radeyah, I got
both Anvils in my opening crypt draw - and with the size of the vamps,
I can't afford to spend time fishing early on. You pretty much have
to have four guys out and abusing things as fast as possible.

This version includes Brujah Anti's, but they're not totally
necessary, they just save that pesky duplicate vampire problem. You
could dupe Anvil, Volker, Black Cat, and assorted others as needed to
make this a pure Brujah deck. Losing Jacko and his free additional
strike is always a shame (since he minion taps so well) but, ah well.
Akram's free Psyche is just lovely in this, too. =)

Library: (90 cards)
8 Blur
10 Bum's Rush
6 Flash
3 Haven Uncovered
1 Lightning Reflexes
5 Minion Tap
3 Potence
8 Psyche
4 Pursuit
2 Quickness
4 Sacrament of Carnage
7 Taste of Vitae
13 Thrown Gate
16 Thrown Sewer Lid

Pretty simple here. Use the Gates, Flashes, and Pursuits for
maneuvers if they block a Rush, otherwise they're just more strike
cards - no big deal. Go to range, Blur, and toss whatever strike
cards you need. Do the math carefully, since you'll be going through
strike cards like water and don't want to catch yourself short. You
will probably have plenty of Psyche! handy to deal with S:CE as
needed. The Minion Taps are absolutely vital if you're going to
survive - don't be scared to Tap yourself down to 1 blood for a Blur
and go into combat hoping for a Taste, because the lack of ranged
combat in general means your guys don't take damage much. The goofy
Sabbat cards (pursuit, quickness, lightning reflexes) can be replaced
by Blurs or Flashes as need be - they just provide a bit of variance
and flavor in maneuvers, etc. There could be more Rushes, but your
guys will need to bleed a lot more since there are fewer of them -
might as well take the "Block me Please" attitude towards your prey,
and use the Rushes on your predator.

You usually end up donating one VP to your grand-predator with this
deck because of its slow nature. Oops. =)

-- Derek
(replying by email? remove the nospam from my domain :)

Ouch. Potence combat suffers the worst from a 6CL. Fortunately, some
of the annoying aspects involved are mitigated by your friends having
to use a 6CL too, but ... ouch.

>and gates (Magnums, Deer Rifles, Grenades, RPG?), but of course that gets
>pricey (Black Cat to the rescue!). With that in mind, how does this deck
>look (I haven't created a crypt yet):

With that in mind, note that weapons are worse than a tossed lid in
three ways: (1) requires an action to equip the weapon, (2) weapons
are more easily hosed than strike cards, being vulnerable to steals
and the like, and (3) weapons cost pool, Black Cat or not.

>Masters:
>
>5xBlood Doll
>3xMinion Tap
>Barrens
>Elder Library
>FotBoN
>3xCelerity
>3xPotence
>3xObfuscate (These would change depending on the crypt)
>3xHaven Uncovered

3xOBF why? =) Other than that, a total of 20 masters - a bit master
heavy, esp. for a combat deck, but you may get away with it with stuff
being less card intensive.

>Equipment:
>
>2xIR Goggles

Bag these. It's an EXTRA equip action that your boys just don't
need... guys who are tossing objects should use Flash, and guys with
guns won't need a spare maneuver THAT often if at all.

>3x.44 Magnum
>3xDeer Rifle

Bag these, too. 1 point of damage per shot is going to make Emerson
Bridges laugh at you even if you DO blur and hit him twice more.
Replace with 3 more .44s :) (Sure, it's great to guarantee you get to
long range, but you pretty much HAVE to chunk two lids at him after
that in order to make him feel it. And you only have six lids.)

>1xBomb (just for fun when I have a Taste)

You can't Taste if you're going to torpor as well... probably not a
good idea.

>6xGrenade

Bag these. Way too many equip actions, and they go AWAY after you use
them. Icky icky.

>2xRPG Launcher

Entertaining if you can get it to work. =) Probably easier under a
6CL where presses are a little more functional.

>General:
>
>6xBum's Rush

...6xAmbush as well? (You hafta get the Rush actions from SOMEWHERE.)

>4xTaste of Vitae
>
>Celerity:
>
>2xAcrobatics

When you're at long range you won't need to dodge before striking.

>4xBlur
>2xFast hands

Do you see -that- many weapons out there? I suppose you hafta have
them handy to steal your own back, maybe. =)

>3xFlash

6xFlash. *the* celerity card.

>3xNimble Feet
>6xPsyche!
>2xPursuit
>2xSide Strike

again, you don't need to dodge at long range usually - pull the 4
dodge options and put in 3 more Flash and 1 more Blur.

>Potence:
>
>6xSacrament of Carnage
>6xThrown Gate
>6xThrown Sewer Lid
>2xIncreased Strength (wish I had more!)
>3xWell-Aimed Car

More presses will be necessary to use these, even with the freebies
you get from the Lids, Flash, and Nimble Feet. =) Maybe more nimble
feet.

>97
>Obfuscate:
>
>4xHidden Lurker
>6xDisguised Weapon
>2xConcealed Weapon
>4xSacrificial Lamb
>2xLost in Crowds
>2xCloak the gathering
>2xFaceless Night (just in case I need stealth to equip or for Sac. Lamb)

Just say "no" to this angle. It increases your library needlessly,
ensuring that you won't be drawing all the weapons, potence cards, and
celerity cards that you really WANT to have. With only a SMALL bit of
luck, you'll be taking an equip action on a .44, get blocked, and be
able to smack the guy with a Lid and a Car - discouraging people from
ever blocking you again. :) The best defense is sometimes a superior
offense.

>Auspex(if crypt allows):
>
>4xFast Reaction
>6xTelepathic Counter (for stealth bleeds)

AUS/POT is not something I recall seeing any vampires below a 9 cap
with. I could look it up, but it's just ugly to try to get it to
work. =) Better toss these. =) If you must find a way to deal with
stealth bleeds, look for guys with DOM/POT - Donal O'Connor, Constanza
Vinti, and the like. Then use Redirections. :)

>129 Library Cards (small compared to my opponents :)) )
>
>Could a deck like this possibly work? Obviously, the biggest prblem would
>be finding a cheap enough crypt to afford the weapons....any ideas?

With 129 library cards and a 6CL, you will have a heckuva time drawing
what you need when you need it. Those two really work against each
other in that respect.

Affording the weapons is even worse - to make POT/CEL work you hafta
have vampires right around 5-cap. It might be better to go for an
all-CEL, all-guns style, which lets you get much lower on the vampire
capacity front and still gives you access to most of the cards. Of
course, you DO lose the Potence toys, but ... just another angle.


